_comment: Findings from running the colour probe matrix on real hardware.
This file is committed BACK to the branch by the machine that ran the
matrix, so results travel with the code that produced them.
Run the host side with:   capenc variant=<id> ...
Run the Deck side with:   arcen-deck probe-matrix
Every row starts as "untested". A row that FAILS is a finding and should
be recorded as such -- do not delete it. A row left "untested" is an
assumption, which is exactly what this matrix exists to eliminate.
Free-text notes about anything visually wrong (banding, crushed blacks,
colour cast, chroma fringing on text) are as valuable as the numbers.

results.question: Control: the format Arcen ships today. Must keep working.
results.notes: Windows NVENC initialised and VideoToolbox required-hardware session succeeded. Five-pattern end-to-end maxima: grey_ramp=2, shadow_highlight_wedge=2, saturated_primaries=1, chroma_detail=2, full_gamut_noise=255. The noise result includes lossy codec quantisation and is not the pure-transform figure.

results.question: Does the full-range flag survive host VUI -> stream -> VideoToolbox?
results.notes: Full-range VUI survived NVENC -> elementary stream -> VideoToolbox and selected 444f. Five-pattern maxima: grey_ramp=0, shadow_highlight_wedge=1, saturated_primaries=1, chroma_detail=3, full_gamut_noise=252.

results.question: THE TARGET. Does VideoToolbox decode 10-bit HEVC Rext, and in hardware?
results.notes: Target row succeeded in a required-hardware VideoToolbox session and delivered xf44. Five-pattern maxima: grey_ramp=0, shadow_highlight_wedge=1, saturated_primaries=0, chroma_detail=1, full_gamut_noise=252. A live pier-windows.example.internal session on its configured GRID V100D-16Q also logged variant=hevc-444-10-full-bt709, full-range VUI and READY bit_depth=10 range=full; Deck displayed the desktop and reported negotiated exactly as requested. Retest on pier-linux.example.internal's GRID V100D-16Q at 1d202cc: the Linux matrix initialised both HEVC 4:4:4 and 4:2:0 10-bit rows; ffprobe reported Rext yuv444p10le full-range BT.709; the corrected per-frame wire flags made Deck receive xf44-full, decode 1800x1130 in hardware, and report negotiated exactly as requested.

results.question: Isolates the range change from the depth change at 10-bit.
results.notes: Required-hardware VideoToolbox decode succeeded and selected x444. Five-pattern maxima: grey_ramp=0, shadow_highlight_wedge=1, saturated_primaries=0, chroma_detail=1, full_gamut_noise=255.

results.question: Main 10 fallback if Rext 10-bit does not decode. Apple documents Main 10.
results.notes: Main 10 fallback succeeded in required-hardware VideoToolbox and selected xf20. Five-pattern maxima: grey_ramp=1, shadow_highlight_wedge=1, saturated_primaries=0, chroma_detail=146, full_gamut_noise=255; the chroma-detail loss is the expected 4:2:0 consequence.

results.question: Cheapest possible full-range win, for the widest client set.
results.notes: Both Windows NVENC and the MF encoder initialised this row; the recorded burst is NVENC. Required-hardware VideoToolbox decode selected 420f. Five-pattern maxima: grey_ramp=1, shadow_highlight_wedge=0, saturated_primaries=1, chroma_detail=146, full_gamut_noise=255.

results.question: Does VideoToolbox decode H.264 High 4:4:4 Predictive at all? Undocumented.
results.notes: Contrary to the expected failure, Apple M4 Pro VideoToolbox decoded H.264 High 4:4:4 Predictive in a required-hardware session and delivered 444f. Five-pattern maxima: grey_ramp=1, shadow_highlight_wedge=0, saturated_primaries=1, chroma_detail=3, full_gamut_noise=225.

results.question: HEVC 4:2:2 is Blackwell-only on the encode side. Free to attempt elsewhere.
results.encoder_error: NVENC 4:2:2 buffer formats (NV16/P210) are absent from these vendored bindings and arcen_media has no BGRA -> 4:2:2 conversion; ChromaSubsampling::Yuv422 cannot reach this encoder
results.notes: Not attempted in VideoToolbox because the host produced no bitstream. The blocker is currently Arcen's unwired 4:2:2 surface/conversion path, before any Blackwell capability question can be measured.

results.question: Can a GBR identity-matrix stream survive CoreVideo, which has no identity constant?
results.notes: Required-hardware VideoToolbox accepted the identity stream and delivered xf44, but CoreMedia exposed no matrix extension. Five-pattern maxima: grey_ramp=1, shadow_highlight_wedge=2, saturated_primaries=0, chroma_detail=3, full_gamut_noise=246. The missing matrix means this remains a probe result, not a shippable identity path.

results.question: Is hardware AV1 real on BOTH ends? NVENC Ada+ encode plus Apple M3+ decode. This is the row the royalty question turns on.
results.notes: L40S NVENC produced a real 3008x1692 AV1 Main 4:2:0 8-bit stream. M4 Pro VideoToolbox reported hardware decode and delivered full-range 420f. The FPS/bitrate values are medians from the matched live YouTube workload, not the synthetic round-trip harness. Auth-time Performance intent later selected this row automatically on the same unpinned host.

results.question: Hardware AV1 at 10-bit on both ends. NVENC AV1 Main covers 8 and 10-bit.
results.notes: L40S NVENC initialization succeeded for AV1 Main 4:2:0 10-bit with the P010 surface. A real M4 decode run remains pending; no delivered pixel format or hardware-decode claim is inferred from initialization alone.

results.question: Software tier. Not NVENC-encodable and not macOS hardware-decodable.
results.notes: NVENC exposes AV1 Main profile only, so hardware rejects 4:4:4. The probe-only rav1e feature can produce this software row, but no product Pier selects it and Deck has no software AV1 decoder. No hardware claim is inferred.

results.question: The only 12-bit route that exists anywhere in the product.
results.notes: capenc has no rav1e dispatch and Deck's current probe harness has no AV1 parameter-set construction path. NVENC cannot encode 12-bit at any subsampling.

field_reference.encoder_error: Exact NVENC/encoder status string when init failed, else null.
field_reference.delivered_pixel_format: The CVPixelBuffer FourCC actually delivered, e.g. xf44.
field_reference.color_extensions_attached: What CMFormatDescriptionGetExtensions() reported, so inferred-vs-set can be compared.
field_reference.roundtrip_max_error: Per-channel MAX error of the injected test pattern, 0-255 scale. 0 means exact. This is an END-TO-END figure and therefore includes codec quantisation loss -- it is NOT the same as the pure colour-conversion error asserted in arcen-media unit tests, which is exactly 0 for 10-bit full range.
field_reference.roundtrip_mean_error: Per-channel MEAN error over the same comparison. Reported alongside the max because a mean hides a single wrong pixel on a matte edge, which is the defect that matters.
field_reference.roundtrip_pattern: Which TestPattern was injected (grey_ramp, shadow_highlight_wedge, saturated_primaries, chroma_detail, full_gamut_noise). Null when no round-trip run was performed.
